en.name: Prophet Muhammad (saws)
en.title: Al-Mustafa (The Chosen One), Khatam al-Anbiya
en.biography: The final Prophet and Messenger of Allah, sent as a mercy to all creation (Rahmatan lil-'Alamin). Born in Mecca into the noble Banu Hashim clan, he was known as Al-Amin (the Trustworthy) even before receiving divine revelation at Cave Hira at age 40. He established Islam, unified Arabia under divine monotheism, received the Holy Qur'an over 23 years, and appointed Imam Ali (as) as his successor at Ghadir Khumm before passing away in Medina.

en.name: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as)
en.title: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful), Asadullah
en.born: 13 Rajab (inside the Holy Kaaba, Mecca, 600 CE)
en.martyrdom: 21 Ramadan, 40 AH (struck on 19th Ramadan in Kufa Mosque)
en.biography: The cousin and son-in-law of Prophet Muhammad (saws), born uniquely inside the Holy Kaaba. He was the first male to accept Islam, the invincible hero of every battle (Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, Khaybar), the fountainhead of wisdom, and the first Infallible Imam appointed at Ghadir Khumm. He ruled as Caliph with absolute justice, refusing corruption, before being martyred while prostrating in Fajr prayer by Ibn Muljam.

She is the core of the Verse of Purity (Ayat al-Tathir) and Mubahalah. Renowned for her intense devotion, piety, charity, and the famous Khutba al-Fadakiya sermon defending divine succession and truth. She passed away shortly after her father due to grief and injuries.

en.title: Al-Mujtaba (The Chosen), Karim Ahlul Bayt (Generous One)
en.biography: The second Infallible Imam and eldest grandson of Prophet Muhammad (saws), who named him and praised him as 'Leader of the Youths of Paradise'. Known for his unparalleled generosity—donating his entire wealth multiple times—he assumed the Caliphate after Imam Ali (as). Facing widespread betrayal and corruption, he signed a strategic Peace Treaty with Mu'awiyah to preserve the blood of Muslims and expose hypocrisy. He was eventually poisoned in Medina.

en.name: Imam Hussain ibn Ali (as)
en.title: Sayyid al-Shuhada (Master of Martyrs), Aba Abdillah
en.biography: The third Infallible Imam and younger grandson of Prophet Muhammad (saws). When Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah demanded allegiance to legitimize despotic tyranny, Imam Hussain stood firm, declaring: 'A person like me cannot pay allegiance to a person like him.' He journeyed to Karbala with his family and 72 loyal companions, where they were besieged, denied water for 3 days, and massacred on the Day of Ashura. His sacrifice revived Islam for all time.

en.name: Imam Ali ibn al-Hussain (as)
en.title: Zayn al-Abidin (Ornament of Worshippers), Al-Sajjad
en.biography: The fourth Infallible Imam, survivor of Karbala who witnessed the martyrdom of his father and brothers. Despite being gravely ill during Ashura, he became the protector of the captive women and children, delivering legendary speeches in Kufa and Yazid's palace in Damascus that shattered Umayyad propaganda. He rebuilt Islamic spirituality through profound supplications, authoring Al-Sahifa al-Sajjadiyya and Risalat al-Huquq (Treatise on Rights).

en.name: Imam Muhammad ibn Ali (as)
en.title: Al-Baqir (Splitter / Revealer of Knowledge)
en.biography: The fifth Infallible Imam, son of Imam Sajjad and grandson of Imam Hasan (through his mother). Prophet Muhammad (saws) had sent him greetings via the companion Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari. Taking advantage of the weakening Umayyad dynasty, he opened the first major Islamic university in Medina, unraveling deep Qur'anic sciences, jurisprudence, medicine, and theology. He was poisoned by Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik.

en.name: Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (as)
en.title: Al-Sadiq (The Truthful), Founder of Ja'fari School
en.biography: The sixth Infallible Imam, born on the exact birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad (saws). He expanded the Medina University into a global center of knowledge, teaching over 4,000 students in jurisprudence, chemistry, astronomy, philosophy, and ethics—including Jabir ibn Hayyan (Father of Chemistry), Abu Hanifa, and Malik ibn Anas. Shia jurisprudence is called Fiqh al-Ja'fari in his honor. He was poisoned by Abbassid caliph Mansur al-Dawanaqi.

en.name: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (as)
en.title: Al-Kadhim (Restrainer of Anger), Bāb al-Hawā'ij
en.biography: The seventh Infallible Imam, famous for his extreme patience, continuous worship, and swallowing his anger (hence Al-Kadhim). He spent much of his Imamate under imprisonment in brutal Abbassid dungeons under Caliph Harun al-Rashid. Even in pitch-black underground cells, he spent every moment in Sajdah and gratitude. He is venerated as Bāb al-Hawā'ij (Gate to Fulfilling Needs). Poisoned on the bridge of Baghdad.

sayings: Whoever has no intellect has no faith, and whoever has no faith has no future.
Work for your worldly life as if you will live forever, and work for your Hereafter as if you will die tomorrow.
Indeed Allah has two proofs over mankind: an apparent proof (the Prophets & Imams) and a hidden proof (the Intellect).

اعمَل لِدُنياكَ كأنَّكَ تَعيشُ أبَداً، واعمَل لآخِرَتِكَ كأنَّكَ تَموتُ غَداً.

en.name: Imam Ali ibn Musa (as)
en.title: Al-Ridha (The Pleasing/Appointed One), Damin al-Ahoo
en.biography: The eighth Infallible Imam, forced by Abbasid Caliph Ma'mun to relocate from Medina to Tus (Khorasan) and conditionally accept heir-apparency. In Nishapur, he narrated the famous Hadith Silsilat al-Dhahab (Golden Chain of Transmission). He engaged in grand interfaith debates organized by Ma'mun with Jewish, Christian, Zoroastrian, and Sabian scholars, universally proving the supreme intellect of Islam. Poisoned with grapes by Ma'mun.

sayings: Faith is a declaration with the tongue, knowledge in the heart, and action with the limbs.
The benchmark of intellect is treating people with kindness and affection after faith in God.
Whoever visits my shrine despite the distance, I will come to their rescue on three terrifying occasions on Judgment Day.

en.biography: The ninth Infallible Imam, who assumed the divine leadership at the young age of 7 following his father's martyrdom. In a historic grand debate organized by Caliph Ma'mun, the young Imam answered 30,000 complex legal questions posed by Chief Justice Yahya ibn Aktham, leaving scholars in absolute awe. Known for his legendary generosity (Al-Jawad), he was martyred at the young age of 25 in Baghdad.

en.name: Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (ajtf)
en.title: Al-Mahdi (The Guided), Al-Qa'im (The Risen), Al-Hujjah, Imam al-Zaman
en.martyrdom: Alive in Occultation (Promised Savior of Humanity)
en.biography: The twelfth and current Infallible Imam, born in Samarra. Following his father's martyrdom, he entered the Minor Occultation (Ghaybah al-Sughra, 260–329 AH), guiding the Shia through Four Special Deputies (Nawwab al-Arba'ah). In 329 AH, he entered the Major Occultation (Ghaybah al-Kubra). He lives among humanity unseen, guiding the faithful, and will reappear alongside Jesus Christ (isa as) to fill the earth with peace, equity, and divine justice.
